enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . ...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 537 AM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

 - Slight chance of showers or thunderstorms this afternoon across
   the Gila region and Hudspeth County. 

 - Otherwise mostly dry seasonable temperatures Tuesday and
   Wednesday.

 - Cool blast of air with windy to very windy conditions looks
   increasingly likely Thursday night into Friday. Well below 
   normal temperatures for Friday and the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1030 PM MDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Long wave UL trough covers roughly the western half of the CONUS
with a closed low over Eastern OR. Somewhere embedded in that
trough is the remnants of Rachel. Closer to home, a band of
showers and a few thunderstorms are moving through the CWA with
activity gradually waning and exiting, leaving most of us dry
overnight. The large-scale trough sticks around for Monday, but we
lose any meaningful dynamics. Monday will be warm and breezy.
Moisture, associated with Hurricane Simon, will be pulled
northward thanks to the trough, and by Monday evening there will
be a low chance for showers/storms across Hudspeth County as most
of any moisture associated with Simon stays east of the area. We
will see another, stronger wave of moisture on Tuesday, but again,
much of the moisture will stay east, only giving Hudspeth County a
chance for showers and storms. 

By Wednesday the main UL low (same one that is now over Oregon)
will exit into the Plains, completely placing Southern NM and Far
West Texas in the dry slot, behind a Pacific front. This will
bring seasonal temperatures for Wednesday and Thursday. 

The aforementioned UL low will also send cooler air southward in 
its wake. The GFS is a tad quicker than Euro with the front, but
in any case, winds will become gusty behind the front, especially
for West Slope areas beginning Thursday evening. Current operational
NBM shows Wind Advisory and High Wind Warning level winds with 
this front, so that will need to be closely monitored. GFS bufkit
soundings also very much supports this forecast with many of our
west slope locations showing a greater than 50% chance of
exceeding 50 MPH gusts. Friday will be a much cooler day with 
highs around 15 degrees below normal. It will feel a bit brisk! 

A piece of the trough breaks off on Thursday, and the GFS and 
Euro show a broad closed low forming off the Baja Coast by Friday 
with moisture being drawn northward. This moisture is, checks and 
rechecks model data, associated with Simon, which manages to 
survive having part of it sheared off earlier in the week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 537 AM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

VRF conditions through the period with SCT-BKN080 SCT-BKN150.
After 18Z...an isolated BKN060 -SHRA possible over the Gila/Black
Range. After 23Z...an isolated BKN070CB -TSRA possible over
Hudspeth County. Winds this afternoon southwest 10-15G25 knots
diminishing by mid evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 537 AM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

Mostly dry today through Wednesday. A few showers possible this
afternoon over the Gila. Only significant feature is a back door
cold front schedule to push in from the east Thursday night. This
will bring a wind shift to the east accompanied by strong, gusty
winds Thursday night through Friday. Places along the south with 
the Intl Border could see gusts to 50 mph or greater, with the 
peak winds Thursday night into Friday morning. Humidity will
remain well above critical thresholds during these winds. Seasonable
temperatures mid week before this front will drop to well below 
normal for Friday and the weekend. 

Min RH: Lowlands 25-35% today and Tuesday, decreasing to 18-25% 
Wednesday and Thursday. Mountains 35-50% today and Tuesday, 
decreasing to 20-35% Wednesday and Thursday. Vent rate good-very
good today and Tuesday, becoming fair-good Wednesday and Thursday.
